regulars.name: Bilal
regulars.line: Do cup, jaldi! The rickshaw is double parked.
levels: Bilal waves from his rickshaw as he passes.
Bilal tells his passengers to try your chai.
Bilal has painted your thela's name on his rickshaw.

regulars.name: Pappu
regulars.line: Akhbar le lo! And one chai, Bhai.
levels: Pappu leaves you a free paper.
Pappu shouts your name with the headlines.
Pappu says he will open a thela like yours one day.

regulars.name: Saima Baji
regulars.line: Forty copies to check before tomorrow. Chai, please.
levels: Saima Baji brings her colleagues.
Saima Baji's class wrote essays about Burns Road.
Saima Baji calls your chai "the best grade in Karachi".

regulars.name: Hamza
regulars.line: Exam tomorrow. Tonight, only bun kabab.
levels: Hamza passed his exam and gives the credit to you.
Hamza brings his whole study group.
Hamza made Burns Road the background of his final project.

regulars.name: Akhtar Sahab
regulars.line: Same as always, beta. The bank closed late again.
levels: Akhtar Sahab sets his watch by your kettle.
Akhtar Sahab recommends you to every customer at his counter.
Akhtar Sahab says your galla is better kept than his bank's.

regulars.name: The Yusuf family
regulars.line: Bachon ko Burns Road dikhana tha. Three bun kababs!
levels: The Yusuf children wave at you from the car.
The Yusufs bring their cousins from Hyderabad.
The Yusufs celebrated an engagement at your stall.

regulars.name: Rehana Khala
regulars.line: Your Dada used to save me the first dahi baray. Do you?
levels: Rehana Khala tells everyone you are "a good boy" or "a good girl".
Rehana Khala sends her neighbours.
Rehana Khala brought you mithai from her daughter's wedding.

regulars.name: Constable Ghafoor
levels: Ghafoor keeps an eye on your thela at night.
Ghafoor chases off the man selling fake "Asli Burns Road" signs.
Ghafoor says Burns Road is quieter when your lamp is on.

pages.title: Elaichi chai
pages.text: Crush the elaichi, never grind it. Let it boil with the leaves, not after. Patience makes colour.

pages.title: The shami secret
pages.text: A spoon of chana daal soaked overnight, and the onion goes in raw. The tawa should hiss, not shout.

pages.title: Nihari, 1975
pages.text: Start the deg at Isha. Bone marrow, nalli, and a ladle of last night's tari. Never rush the night.

pages.title: Rickshaw hours
pages.text: The drivers have five minutes. Have the glass poured before they ask.
pages.hint: A morning regular with a rickshaw

pages.title: The morning paper
pages.text: The boy who sells the news sells your name too. Feed him well.

pages.title: A teacher's tea
pages.text: Teachers tip in kindness and in customers. Remember their names.
pages.hint: A teacher with copies to check

pages.title: Exam nights
pages.text: Students eat when they are worried. Make the bun soft and the chutney sharp.

pages.title: The clerk's clock
pages.text: Office men come at the same minute every day. Be ready at that minute.

pages.title: The family table
pages.text: Families stay when the children are happy. Keep the chairs clean and the line short.

pages.title: Khala's dahi
pages.text: Soak the baray in warm water first, then the dahi. Never the other way round.
pages.hint: An aunty who knew your Dada

pages.title: Buy what you sell
pages.text: The milkman's son taught me: buy for the day you will have, not the day you hope for.

pages.title: The samosa fold
pages.text: Three folds, not two. Seal with flour paste and fry on a low flame until it sings.

cards.title: The beat constable
cards.text: Constable Ghafoor leans on your thela. "Chai to milegi na? The area is mine, after all."

options.label: Chai on the house
options.result: He sips, nods, and moves the other hawkers along for the evening.

options.label: Politely charge him
options.result: He pays, grumbling. An honest galla, an honest chai.

cards.title: A food blogger
cards.text: A girl with a phone on a stick: "Can I film your thela for my 40k followers? One free plate?"

options.label: Free plate, film away
options.result: The video goes round Karachi by night. She leaves you a tip: an old samosa trick.

options.label: Everyone pays, beta
options.result: She pays and films anyway. A smaller video, but an honest one.

cards.title: Flood relief
cards.text: Students are collecting for families hit by the floods in Sindh.

options.label: Give Rs 2,000
options.result: They write your thela's name on their banner. Burns Road notices.

options.label: Free chai for the volunteers
options.result: Ten cups for ten tired students. They promise to come back.

options.label: Not today
options.result: They thank you anyway and move down the road.

cards.title: A wedding order
cards.text: The groom's uncle from the next street: "Sixty bun kababs for the mehndi. Half the money now, the rest on Sunday."

options.label: Take the order
options.result: A long night on the tawa, and Rs 3,000 in the galla. The rest comes Sunday, inshallah.

options.label: Too big for my thela
options.result: He goes to Khan Broast. Maybe next time.

cards.title: The kiryana's offer
cards.text: The corner shop: "Take a week of milk now, Rs 3,000, and I'll knock off ten percent."

options.label: Stock up
options.result: Crates of milk stacked behind the thela. Mind it does not spoil.

cards.title: Fifty rupees short
cards.text: A student counts his coins twice. He is Rs 50 short for his bun kabab.

options.label: Let it go
options.result: "I'll pay you back, Bhai!" He tells his whole hostel.

options.label: Half a plate, then
options.result: He takes the half plate and smiles anyway.

cards.title: The broast man's offer
cards.text: The Khan Broast owner: "No price war, yaar. Let's both stay out of each other's way tonight."

options.label: Shake hands
options.result: His grill stays quiet tonight; your line grows.

options.label: May the best plate win
options.result: He laughs. The street loves a rivalry.

cards.title: A TV crew
cards.text: A TV crew is filming "Karachi's food streets". The anchor wants nihari on camera.

options.label: Serve the crew
options.result: Your deg on national television. The phones won't stop.

quests.title: Dada's elaichi chai
quests.intro: Your Dada's chai had something mine never did. Serve 60 cups and maybe you will find his secret. He wrote everything down, you know.
quests.outro: There! A page fell out of the book: "Elaichi chai". Forty years I waited to taste that again.

quests.title: The shami secret
quests.intro: In 1971 your Dada fed half of Burns Road on credit. His bun kabab was why they paid him back. Serve 120 and earn the next page.
quests.outro: Chana daal! Of course. Your Dada was laughing at all of us. Keep the page safe.

quests.title: Nihari, 1975
quests.intro: The deg is lit again. The year I first sat here, your Dada made nihari that people queued for at Fajr. Serve 40 plates.
quests.outro: The taste of 1975. You have his hands, beta. Burns Road will know your name soon.

quests.title: Burns Road knows your name
quests.intro: One last thing for this old man: two stars of Shohrat. Then I will tell you what your Dada said to me the night he closed.
quests.outro: He said: "Rasheed, the thela will come back. Wait for it." I waited, beta. It was worth it.
